asr_text: On September 3rd, 2026, a medical journal published a new gene treatment for hard-to-treat autoimmune diseases of the nervous system. The study included 16 people, seven with progressive multiple sclerosis and three each with MOG antibody-associated disease, generalized myasthenia gravis, and idiopathic inflammatory muscle disease. The unusual part was where the treatment was made. Instead of removing a patient's immune cells, changing them in a laboratory, and putting them back, researchers gave one intravenous dose of a disabled gene carrier. It delivered a gene for CD19-targeting CAR T cells into the patient's own T cells inside the body.
